claim: Log-loss of a predictor equals code length; arithmetic coding turns any predictor into a lossless compressor, and next-token loss over in-context examples is prequential code length.
agent_test: Score each candidate rule by summed log-loss on the examples in order (prequential), not by prose length; check it ranks rules the same as held-out accuracy.

claim: Ideal (Kolmogorov) MDL is uncomputable and depends on the description language; for short data the language constant can dominate, so practical MDL restricts the language.
agent_test: When ranking rules by length, fix one description language in code and test that the winner does not flip when the language changes.

claim: Raw compression rate of a big LM hides its own size. Counting parameters (two-part code), pretrained foundation models give adjusted rates above 100% offline, yet prequential coding makes deep nets cheap (MNIST about 4.1 kbits vs 199 kbits uniform). Whether the model costs anything depends on the code type.
agent_test: Do not count a frozen model as free: compare length-based selection with and without a per-rule cost for rule size, at equal tokens.

claim: Bits per character of a base LM on fresh text is almost linear in its benchmark scores across 31 LLMs and 12 benchmarks (Pearson about -0.93 overall, about -0.95 per domain; per benchmark -0.881 HellaSwag, -0.951 TriviaQA, -0.890 MMLU, -0.946 DS-1000).
agent_test: Not a scaffold test. Sanity check only: a cheap proxy to compare base models before costly agent evals.

claim: The compression-intelligence line breaks with contamination (three Qwen models above the fit on GSM8K/MATH), weakens when the corpus does not match the skill, applies only to base and well-trained LMs, and the corpus needs only about 3M characters to saturate.
agent_test: If likelihood of our own traces is used as a quality signal, test it on held-out tasks first for leakage.

claim: Prompted frontier LLMs are poor at writing the shortest program that reproduces data: on length-128 sequences Llama-3.1-405B and GPT-4o err on average over 78% and 40% on natural data (abstract: 66% and 45% on synthetic; body text says 65% and 55%). Every prompted model has precision above 1 (longer than gzip).
agent_test: Ask the agent for a program that prints task data and compare its length with gzip; expect failure, so do not trust a self-claimed short rule.

claim: Over 95% of correct programs on natural data in the Kolmogorov Test just repeat the input (20% on synthetic); chain of thought and execution feedback help little (Llama CoT -1.3, -5.1, +2.1 points for 8B, 70B, 405B).
agent_test: Check that candidate rules are shorter than the data they explain before counting a pass; log the rule-to-data length ratio.

claim: Library learning by compressing solved programs improves program synthesis: DreamCoder 3.7% to 79.6% on list tasks, search time 235 s to 40 s, 93% of 60 physics laws; a memorise-without-compressing control solves fewer held-out tasks; LILO (MDL compression via Stitch plus an LLM) adds +33.14 REGEX, +2.26 CLEVR, +20.42 LOGO over DreamCoder; OOPS prefix reuse sped search 1000x.
agent_test: Store verified solution fragments as reusable named helpers in memory; test at equal tokens on a task family with shared subroutines versus storing whole past solutions.

claim: Compressed abstractions are not enough for an LLM without names and docs: Stitch compression alone lowers the LLM solver by 30.60 (REGEX), 2.91 (CLEVR), 11.11 (LOGO) points; auto-written docs recover +9.73, +2.27, +0.00.
agent_test: When saving a learned helper to memory, store a name and a one-line doc with it; compare recall-and-use with and without the doc.

claim: LLM-proposed hypothesis then program then execution check beats direct prompting on ARC: 17% direct, 23% program only, 30% summarised hypotheses, 33% human-selected, 45% human-written (100 tasks, GPT-4, 64 programs, 3 feedback rounds); Greenblatt LLM program sampling scored 43% private, and Li et al. induction rises with samples (35.25% at 20k votes on Potpourri).
agent_test: At equal tokens compare: direct answer, N programs, and hypothesis-then-program with execution on the given examples.

claim: Programs that fit all training pairs usually pass the test (GPT-4 setup: one exception in the subset), but in large sampling pools about 9% of fitting samples are false positives, and our own data had two wrong fitting programs. New (gap 2): wider test suites expose failures of programs that pass few tests (EvalPlus: pass@1 down 12.6-18.5% for 2023 models; pass@100 down up to 28.9%). No 2025-2026 rule-induction measurement found.
agent_test: Measure the false-pass rate of fit-the-examples programs on our tasks; add a held-out or mutated-input check and count how many it catches.

claim: Induction (write a program) and transduction (predict the output) solve different ARC tasks; per-task assignment is stable across seeds (p<.004). A fallback ensemble beat both in small-compute settings (26.50% vs 18.78% and 15.25%), but with test-time training the ensemble (38.00%) was below transduction alone (43.25%) on ARC-Heavy.
agent_test: Route: try a program first and check it on the examples; if none fits within budget fall back to a direct answer. Test against each alone at equal tokens.

claim: Test-time training on the task's own examples lifts ARC strongly (80-task subset 17.5% to 45.0%; public validation 18.3% to 47.1% for the fine-tuned model, 53.0% on the BARC model, 61.9% ensembled with program synthesis; BBH 10-shot 50.5% to 57.8%); ARChitects scored 53.5% on the private set.
agent_test: Not testable in a prompt-only scaffold (needs weight updates). Closest proxy is in-context accumulation of verified pairs; list as out of scope.

claim: LMs are good rule proposers but poor rule appliers: accuracy falls from over 80% to almost zero on MiniSCAN when the LM applies its own rule instead of a symbolic interpreter; running code gives strong results.
agent_test: Apply a proposed rule by running code, never by asking the model to apply it; compare the two on rule-following tasks.

claim: A pure MDL test-time method with no pretraining (CompressARC, 76K parameters, trained only on the target puzzle) solves 34.75% of ARC-AGI-1 training and 20% of evaluation puzzles at pass@2 (pass@1 30.25% and 18.5%), about 20 minutes per puzzle on an RTX 4070; it cannot count or chain operations.
agent_test: Out of scope for prompting; shows a compression objective alone carries signal, so a code-length tie-break among passing rules is plausible.

claim: Networks trained on random universal-Turing-machine programs approach Bayes-optimal prediction on variable-order Markov sources and transfer to Chomsky tasks, but fail to extend beyond training length (256 to 1024); a similar length limit appears for learned compressors in Deletang et al.
agent_test: Weak relevance. If we build rule-induction tests, include sequences longer than the examples to expose the length cliff.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Prequential (online) code length is a more stable measure of model complexity than accuracy or variational codes: Voita and Titov code lengths separate real from control tasks and ignore seed noise; Blier and Ollivier show short prequential codes; Elmoznino shows prequential ICL prefers simpler functions.
agent_test: Use summed online loss over example order as a selection score and test it against accuracy on held-out items.

claim: A pretrained LLM did not lower prequential code length on Mastermind; it did worse than the empirical-marginal baseline, so ICL in current LLMs may not implement simplicity-preferring inference on every task.
agent_test: Run the same prequential check on our model for one rule-induction family before trusting a length-based selector.

claim: Deep nets prefer simple functions: random-parameter nets favour simple Boolean functions exponentially, and an SGD posterior built from a function prior matches measured nets; the prior depends on architecture so the bias is not universal.
agent_test: Background only. Supports a shorter-rule default prior, not a test.

claim: English-language hypotheses fit human number-game judgments better than Python hypotheses (R2 = .81 with a tuned prior, 8 people); GPT-4's own judgments differed from humans.
agent_test: Compare English versus code hypothesis spaces for the S2 representation step on a small task set.

claim: Bayesian program learning of handwritten characters matched humans in one-shot learning: 20-way one-shot error BPL 3.3% vs humans 4.5% (upper bound), simple ConvNet 13.5%, Siamese ConvNet 8.0% (second-hand from Lake et al. 2019 progress report; Lake 2015 itself not opened). An earlier version of this claim had the 3.3 and 4.5 figures attached to the wrong groups. Later meta-learned nets reached 4.0-6.0% on related variants.
agent_test: Cite the 2019 progress report, not the 2015 paper, until the Science paper is opened.

claim: Brute-force DSL program search (icecuber, 20% private) was overtaken in 2024 by LLM-guided program synthesis and test-time training; prompted models without either scored low (o1-preview 18%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 14% pass@1 on private).
agent_test: Treat program sampling plus execution as the baseline to beat before adding anything compression-based.

claim: On ARC-AGI-2 private (2025 Kaggle), the winners were test-time-trained neural models (NVARC 24.03%, ARChitects 16.53%); CompressARC, a pure MDL test-time method, scored 4% on ARC-AGI-2 vs about 20% on ARC-AGI-1.
agent_test: Treat pure MDL at test time as a niche tool for simple repeated structure, not as a general selector. Next: Do not claim MDL scales; no scaling study exists.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Execution-checked program search with refinement on ARC reaches about 43-52% (SOAR) but its selector is a weighted vote that leaves a 9.5-point average gap to oracle (52.00% vote vs 57.25% oracle).
agent_test: Compare shortest-consistent-program selection against weighted vote on the same sample pool; the room is 5-10 points. Next: Gap 1 still untested directly.

claim: Passing few example-checks is weak evidence of correctness: widening the test suite cuts measured pass rates by 12-19% at pass@1 (EvalPlus, 2023 models) and many CodeContests problems had broken tests; 2025-2026 frontier numbers for rule induction are missing.
agent_test: Hold out or mutate inputs before accepting a program that fits all examples. Next: Add a mutated-input check to S7 and measure the failure rate on our own tasks.

claim: Consensus among programs and generated tests is a strong selector for code (CodeT: HumanEval pass@1 47.0% to 65.8%); no paper tests a length rule against it at equal samples.
agent_test: Baseline for any length-based selection test. Next: Run vote vs shortest-consistent at equal tokens.

claim: A language model's own log-probability is a biased length measure for ranking programs: it prefers short degenerate programs, and length normalisation overcorrects (Coder-Reviewer wins 43 of 48 dataset-model pairs).
agent_test: Compute program length in a fixed language (token or tree count), never from model log-probs. Next: Check on current models; evidence is from 2022 models.

claim: LLM library-learning gains may not come from reuse: LEGO-Prover reused 1 lemma once; TroVE had 3 reuses in 3,201 questions; removing cross-problem sharing lost 1 question. ReGAL shows real gains (+8.1 to +26.1 points, CodeLlama-13B) when tasks share subroutines.
agent_test: Test helper memory against a zero-reuse control at equal tokens. Next: Break-even task count still unknown.

claim: The Kolmogorov Test: o1-mini did not beat GPT-4o on length-128 sequences (Accuracy 57.2 vs 56.5; executable 81.7% vs 89.9%); chain of thought gave no real gain. No o3, Claude or Gemini thinking models were tested in any source found.
agent_test: Do not assume a reasoning model writes shorter programs. Next: Run the test on current models.

claim: The compression-benchmark line (Huang et al.) is stated for base models only; the authors say fine-tuned models are not general-purpose compressors and leave them unstudied.
agent_test: Do not use likelihood as a quality proxy for instruct or reasoning models. Next: Gap 10 remains open.

claim: Human simplicity measures track description length in a fixed small language: Boolean concept difficulty with formula length (41 concept types, Feldman 2000, abstract only) and binary-sequence memory with shortest-formula length (Planton 2021, five experiments).
agent_test: Background support for a short-rule default prior. Next: Replications and LLM-vs-human error patterns not found.
